item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03300","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 120/2 by dividing again to obtain 30, then gives an unsupported final 15.","case2_error":"Reports Pool Supply's 600 pools instead of both stores' combined 800 pools.","reason":"Case 1 miscalculates a correctly written average; case 2 correctly calculates one store's inventory but answers the wrong quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03301","case1_error":"Uses the first day's total 50 flowers as its tulip count instead of 30, double-counting 20 roses.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported revenue of 168 after a correct verbal procedure; the actual revenue is 216.","reason":"Case 1 visibly substitutes the wrong category count. Case 2 shows no numerical calculation explaining its incorrect final number.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03302","case1_error":"Omits Ted's four eaten cookies, reporting 138 instead of 134.","case2_error":"No clear error: 27 follows individual pricing for friends; 25 assumes buying an additional discounted dozen.","reason":"The question does not explicitly require minimizing cost or applying the dozen offer to friends' flowers, making case 2 materially ambiguous.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03303","case1_error":"Treats four bags as four peanuts, omitting the 30 peanuts per bag.","case2_error":"Counts one bag's fuel surcharge per person despite each person bringing two bags.","reason":"Both omit the stated number of items per group when calculating the items' total contribution.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J03304","case1_error":"Invents earnings as bike cost plus repairs, ignores the remaining-fifth constraint, and divides post-repair money by apple price.","case2_error":"Correctly calculates 720 for five days but explicitly returns the daily wage, 144.","reason":"Case 1 constructs erroneous financial relations; case 2 calculates the requested total correctly but chooses a different requested time quantity.","judgment":"different"}]}
